safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.5 to 2.21 days

narrative: Material PL1__ME25B68B shows erratic daily demand (CV=0.60) over 149 working days with 82% non-zero demand days and a Gamma-like distribution. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.42, mean=2.70 days), making them the primary driver of safety stock. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, creating significant stockout exposure. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with SS=573 units and Q=1,329 units achieves the 95% service level while reducing annual costs by 51% through EOQ-optimised batch sizing, constrained to the 1,933-unit storage limit.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint binds: order_quantity reduced from 1,360 (unconstrained) to 1,329 to satisfy SS+Q <= 1933.019
Capacity utilisation is 98.4% — minimal headroom for demand surges; recommend monitoring warehouse utilisation monthly

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has continuously monitored, erratic demand with unstable lead times. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is appropriate because it triggers replenishment precisely when inventory hits the reorder point, avoiding the additional safety stock overhead of periodic review while handling the high demand and lead-time variability through an analytically derived safety stock.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap of 1,933 units forces the order quantity below the unconstrained EOQ. This slightly increases ordering frequency and cost but remains within feasibility. Service level is maintained at 95%. If demand spikes near the reorder point while stock on hand is near maximum, the cap could delay a necessary replenishment — this risk is low but non-zero.
